# Support platform routing fault doubles first-response times to 9.6 hours

*Undocumented rules built by a departed contractor sent widget tickets to the wrong queues*

A fault in the routing rules of a support platform has more than doubled median
first-response time, to 9.6 hours from 4.1 over the past 90 days, and the company
will patch the rules this quarter rather than attempt the full rewrite its
engineers say the system needs.

The rules, written by a contractor who has since left and never documented,
misdirect tickets raised through the company's in-app widget into the wrong
queues. Agents have compensated by re-routing 2,840 tickets by hand over the
period, roughly 18 per cent of everything arriving, at a cost of about four
minutes of additional triage on each one.

Customer satisfaction has fallen in both affected queues, from 4.4 to 3.9 in
billing and from 4.5 to 4.1 in technical. A pricing change introduced in the same
window means the routing fault cannot be isolated as the cause. The company's own
review calls the correlation plausible but unproven, a distinction that matters
because the rewrite is justified partly on satisfaction grounds.

Capacity is the binding constraint. Six weeks of engineering time are available
this quarter, two of which are committed to closing a weekend on-call gap that
left a single engineer covering two of the period's three serious incidents. That
leaves four weeks against an eight-week rewrite, which is why the one-week patch
has been chosen for now and the rewrite deferred to the first quarter.
